data.name: Car windscreen replacement
data.description: Mobile windscreen replacement across Sydney and NSW: the glass your vehicle actually takes, ADAS calibration, and what moves the price. Quoted before we start.

mainEntity.name: How long does a windscreen replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: The fitting itself is usually the shortest part of the visit. What extends it is the adhesive cure time before the car is safe to drive, and recalibration if your vehicle has a camera behind the glass. We give you the full picture when you book, including exactly how long before the car is safe to drive.

mainEntity.name: Can it be done at my home or workplace?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. That is how we do most jobs. We need room to open both front doors and walk the length of the windscreen, and somewhere reasonably sheltered if it is raining hard, because urethane adhesive does not cure properly in the wet.

mainEntity.name: Do you handle the ADAS calibration as well?

acceptedAnswer.text: Where the vehicle requires it, we arrange the calibration as part of the job and coordinate it with the replacement, so you are dealing with one booking rather than chasing a second appointment.

Most comprehensive policies in NSW do, often with a separate glass excess that is lower than the standard excess. Whether it is worth claiming depends on how your excess compares with the cost of the job. Check your policy or ask your insurer. Cover varies.
